items.item_text: Current California Registered Nurse (RN), Nurse Practitioner (NP), and Nurse Practitioner Furnishing (NPF) licensure.
Current national certification as a Pediatric Acute Care Nurse Practitioner.
Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross.
Current Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) certification from the American Heart Association.
Master's degree or higher from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program with a specialty in Pediatric Acute Care.
Minimum two (2) years of experience as an Acute Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner.
Minimum 1 year of pediatric pain management and/or palliative care experience.
Experience managing pain and complex symptom burden in children with serious acute, chronic, or life-limiting illnesses.
Experience facilitating family meetings, goals-of-care discussions, and shared decision-making.
Experience working within an interdisciplinary team that includes physicians, nursing, social work, psychology, child life, rehabilitation services, and spiritual care.

The Pediatric Pain & Palliative Care Nurse Practitioner (NP) is an advanced practice provider who delivers comprehensive, family-centered care to infants, children, adolescents, and young adults with acute, chronic, complex, and life-limiting conditions. As a member of the interdisciplinary Pain & Palliative Care team, the NP provides expert assessment and management of pain and other distressing symptoms, facilitates goals-of-care discussions, supports complex medical decision-making, and promotes quality of life for patients and families.

The NP collaborates with multidisciplinary healthcare teams to address the physical, emotional, psychosocial, and spiritual needs of patients and families through symptom management, care coordination, patient and family education, and interdisciplinary care planning. The NP practices under approved standardized procedures, promotes evidence-based care, and serves as a resource for pain management and palliative care across the continuum of care.
This is a limited appointment (not to exceed 8 months)
